items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Interviewer mentions Andre Hodier coined terms; Interviewee confirms ('Yes, yes, yes') but provides no personal interaction details.

ctx.x: Well, there certainly weren't as many; it's just that they played differently. What they were playing .... if you play a solo and you -- like if you were to play the "St. Louis Blues" , you'd go da dee doo da, but if you said da da dee doo da, da, -- well this is still improvising. Very simply, and you're not running a great deal of changed, but it's still -- you're improvising or
to some degree, you're certainly altering the melody. Would that be synonymous with improvising?
Well, it brings in to question here, two terms that I guess were coined again by Andre Hodier, which he calls the paraphrase, which is what you're describing.
